claims.statement: For every fixed policy with loss in [0,1], |R_Q(pi)-R_P(pi)| <= TV(P,Q); hence joint TV(P,Q)<=rho gives robust target risk <= source risk + rho.
claims.evidence: Bounded-function variational characterization of total variation; proof in REPORT.md.
claims.scope: TV is over the full joint feature-label law. A marginal-only feature divergence does not imply this claim without conditional-label structure.
claims.costs: No density-ratio estimation, target samples, or target labels are used; rho is a supplied valid upper bound.

claims.statement: For a finite M-policy class and n iid fully labeled source examples, empirical risk minimization has target robust risk <= best source risk + 2 sqrt(log(2M/alpha)/(2n)) + rho with probability >=1-alpha.
claims.evidence: Uniform two-sided Hoeffding bound over the finite class and the TV transfer lemma; derivation in REPORT.md.
claims.scope: The bound does not imply an adaptive-acquisition advantage when the baseline may optimize over the same policy class and transcript.

claims.statement: For uniform independent bits (Z0,A,B), Y=A when Z0=0 and Y=B when Z0=1, an ERM over 16 branch-conditioned policies queries exactly two features and has robust target risk <= sqrt(log(16/alpha)/(2n))+rho; every fixed feature subset of size at most two has robust risk at least 1/4. The concrete static rule that queries A and predicts A has exact robust risk 1/4+rho for rho<=3/4.
claims.evidence: Conditional Bayes-error lower bound, finite-class one-sided Hoeffding bound, and a TV reweighting adversary for the concrete static rule; full proof and accounting in REPORT.md.
claims.scope: Advantage is over nonadaptive fixed-subset feature acquisition under a two-query deployment cap. It is not an advantage over adaptive robust ERM with the same policy class.

claims.statement: A feature-marginal TV budget alone cannot bound target classification risk without an assumption on conditional label laws.
claims.evidence: One-point feature space with a deterministic source label 0 and deterministic target label 1 has feature-marginal TV zero and target risk one for a source-perfect predictor.
claims.scope: Exact even when feature marginals are identical.

claims.statement: Positive active learning under distribution shift already has primary-literature guarantees under structural assumptions, including label shift with importance-weight and finite-label identifiability conditions.
evidence: Ben-David et al. (2010), A Theory of Learning from Different Domains, Machine Learning 79:151-175.
Ben-David et al. (2010), Impossibility Theorems for Domain Adaptation, AISTATS/PMLR 9:129-136.
Sugiyama et al. (2007), Covariate Shift Adaptation by Importance Weighted Cross Validation, JMLR 8:985-1005.
Zhao et al. (2021), Active Learning under Label Shift, AISTATS/PMLR 130:3412-3420.
claims.scope: This is a scoped check of cited primary sources, not a complete priority search.

open_obligations: No efficient high-dimensional procedure or finite-sample certificate for the supplied joint-TV radius rho is provided.
No universal adaptivity advantage under divergence budget alone is claimed.
The Boolean witness is not claimed as novel and has not undergone independent proof review or formal-kernel checking.
If only input marginals are controlled, an invariant conditional-label model or target-label access must be added and charged.
